articles.title: India bans import of goods made with forced labour
articles.summary: India has amended its foreign trade policy to ban goods produced using forced labour. This move comes amid a US investigation into forced labour practices globally. The new policy prohibits imports of goods manufactured wholly or in part through forced labour. This prohibition will take effect after a 30-day period from its official gazette publication. The government can issue notifications to ban specific goods based on evidence of forced labour.

articles.title: Textile Circularity Stalls Where Education, Community and Business Fail to Connect
articles.summary: A review of fashion and textile waste management finds that discarded materials are mostly landfilled or incinerated globally. The study reveals that education, community efforts, and small business innovations each contribute to circularity but fail to address the issue alone, pointing to a lack of coordination rather than a lack of knowledge. The textile industry's waste problem persists due to this systemic disconnect.
articles.raw_summary: Fashion and textile waste continues to outpace the systems meant to manage it, with most discarded material still landfilled or incinerated worldwide. A new review examining education, community action and small business innovation finds that each advances circularity on its own, but none closes the gap alone, exposing a coordination failure rather than a knowledge one.

articles.title: Indian Knitwear Gets a Design Overhaul as One Label Rejects Seasonal Limits
articles.summary: Indian knitwear remains largely seasonal, confined to winter essentials and mass production with limited design ambition. Saloni Jain , founder and designer of her eponymous label Saloni Jain , approaches knit as a creative discipline grounded in fibre science and construction logic. Her work in cotton, linen and lyocell reframes knitwear as a year-round design medium for the Indian market.

articles.title: DRP 130726: Urge to set up Statutory River Authority
articles.summary: The South Asia Network on Dams, Rivers and People (SANDRP) has proposed a draft Bill that prioritizes ecological flow in river waters, making it the first charge after emergency drinking water needs. The proposal also suggests that water released to sustain rivers should no longer be recorded as waste or unutilized water in official documents. This aims to address environmental concerns and redefine water management policies in India.
articles.raw_summary: One of the significant provisions of the draft Bill is the declaration that ecological flow should become the first charge on river waters, subordinate only to emergency drinking water requirements. The proposal also states that water released to keep rivers alive should no longer be treated as “waste”, “loss” or “unutilised water” in official records.

articles.title: Flooding Under the Scorching Sun: The Unstudied Crisis of Himalayan Nallahs
articles.summary: Residents of Lindur village in Lahaul, Himalayas, report severe flooding in the Jahlma nallah, exacerbated by extreme heat. Jagdish ji, a local farmer, states, "The sun was so hot, we knew the floods would be coming." The crisis disrupts agriculture and infrastructure, with bridges collapsing and fields inundated. The article underscores the urgent need for studied interventions to address climate-linked disasters in vulnerable Himalayan regions.

articles.title: Mangalam Worldwide commissions 10.4 MW solar project to power steel manufacturing
articles.summary: Mangalam Worldwide Ltd, a Gujarat-based stainless steel manufacturer, commissioned a 10.4 MW ground-mounted captive solar power plant at its Halol facility. This increases the company's total solar capacity to 11.6 MW, aiming to reduce electricity price volatility and enhance export readiness. The project aligns with broader renewable energy adoption trends in India's industrial sector.

The company said the additional renewable energy capacity will help reduce exposure to electricity price volatility and strengthen export readiness for global markets.

articles.title: PM-KUSUM worked. The next chapter has to be about farmer income
articles.summary: The PM-KUSUM scheme, a government initiative, has successfully encouraged farmers to adopt solar energy solutions. The article emphasizes that the next step is to shift farmers from being subsidy beneficiaries to becoming energy producers, a transition that has only just begun. This shift could significantly impact farmer income and India's energy landscape.
articles.raw_summary: The scheme proved farmers will adopt solar. The real prize was always turning the farmer from a subsidy beneficiary into an energy producer - and that is the part we have barely started.

articles.title: What is the Index of Services Production and which sectors does it cover?
articles.summary: India's Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation has launched a new monthly services production index. This experimental index, with 2024-25 as its base year, covers 19 formal services sub-sectors. The first release for April 2026 shows broad-based growth across most services categories.
